how_read: Pages read with scripts/kb/fetch_wiki_live_pages.py (the wiki's page-render call) on the date above; the revision is the one the fetcher printed. Each quote is a sentence or part of a sentence from that page, checked by script to occur in the fetched text.

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A giant Chain Chomp chained to a peg in Bob-omb Battlefield, close to a cell that holds the Power Star of "Behind Chain Chomp's Gate".

from.quote: A giant Chain Chomp
is located on Bob-omb Battlefield in Super Mario 64
It is attached to a peg near a cell with the Power Star of

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: You cannot beat it, since Chain Chomps are almost entirely invincible, but a Bob-omb or a box stuns it for a moment.

from.quote: In Super Mario games, they are almost entirely invincible
A Bob-omb, a box, or a Yoshi's egg in the remake can stun Chain Chomp briefly.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: It lunges at you when you are near and takes three wedges of health on contact. Ground-pound its post three times to free it, and it lunges into the nearby cell and clears the gate for the star.

from.quote: The Chain Chomp lunges at Mario if he is nearby, taking away three wedges of his health on contact.
The Chain Chomp can be freed by ground-pounding its post three times, required for it to lunge into the cell nearby and clear

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A small ghost that follows you in the courtyard of Peach's Castle and in Big Boo's Haunt; touching one takes two wedges of health.

from.quote: Boos (also called Baby Boos) appear in Super Mario 64
Boos are encountered in the courtyard of Peach's Castle and in Big Boo's Haunt.
Boos take away two wedges of health on contact.

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: A punch, a kick or a ground pound defeats it. When you look at one it turns partly see-through; otherwise it is solid and follows you.

from.quote: Boos are defeated from either a punch, a kick, a Pound the Ground attack
When Boos are looked at, they become partially visible, but are fully opaque otherwise and follow the player character.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: Each Boo in the courtyard holds a yellow coin, and each one in Big Boo's Haunt holds a blue coin.

from.quote: The Boos in the courtyard hold a Yellow Coin each, and those in Big Boo's Haunt each have a Blue Coin

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: The giant ghost who owns Big Boo's Haunt and leads the Boos; he is the boss of "Go on a Ghost Hunt", "Ride Big Boo's Merry-Go-Round" and "Big Boo's Balcony", and a touch costs three wedges of health.

from.quote: acting as the Boos' leader
Big Boo makes his debut in Super Mario 64 as the owner of Big Boo's Haunt, being the boss of "Go on a Ghost Hunt", "Ride Big Boo's Merry-Go-Round", and "Big Boo's Balcony".
If this Boo attacks Mario, he loses three wedges of health.

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: He can be hurt only while visible, by ground-pounding him from above or punching him from the side. Three hits defeat him, and he gets smaller and faster after each one.

from.quote: Big Boo can be attacked only when visible, so Mario has to attack this massive ghost by either ground-pounding him from above or punching him from the side. He takes three hits to defeat, becoming smaller and faster after each hit.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: In the first two missions you must defeat several nearby Boos to make him appear; in "Big Boo's Balcony" he is already there. Like a normal Boo he disappears when looked at and shows again when you turn away, and if you leave the area before he is beaten his health resets.

from.quote: For the first two missions, Mario needs to defeat several nearby Boos to make him appear, though for the last one, he is automatically present
Like with the normal Boos, Big Boo disappears when looked at and becomes visible again when Mario turns away.
if the player leaves the area before completely defeating Big Boo, his health resets.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: A Big Boo about twice the size of the other Boos waits in a corner of the castle courtyard, and beating it drops a birdcage that leads to Big Boo's Haunt.

from.quote: In the courtyard itself, it can be found in one of the corners, appearing about twice as large as the other Boos. If Mario defeats it, it drops a birdcage
leading to Big Boo's Haunt.

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A sleepy plant with green lips, found in Whomp's Fortress in the original game, that is always asleep, with a lullaby playing, until you disturb it.

from.quote: They are depicted with green lips in the original version
Piranha Plants appear only in Whomp's Fortress
Piranha Plants have a sleepy nature, which is why they are always found asleep; during this, a lullaby plays.

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: Walk up slowly and it stays asleep; touch it or rush at it and it wakes and bites toward you.

from.quote: When a Piranha Plant is either touched or approached quickly by the player character, it wakes up and starts to bite in the direction of the player character, though they stay asleep if approached slowly.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: A bite takes three points of health, or four if you have lost your cap. A defeated Piranha Plant leaves a blue coin.

from.quote: Piranha Plants take away three health points if they bite the player character, or four if he is without his cap
Defeating certain enemies causes a Blue Coin to appear, including Koopa Troopas, Piranha Plants, Boos

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A common walking bomb that first appears in Bob-omb Battlefield: when it spots you it lights its fuse and rushes at you.

from.quote: Bob-ombs are common enemies in Super Mario 64 and its Nintendo DS version. They first appear on the Bob-omb Battlefield.
When a Bob-omb spots the player, it lights its fuse and then rushes towards them from behind, attempting to damage them when it explodes.

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: Touching one does no harm, but its explosion costs two wedges of health. Kick it, or pick it up from behind and throw it, and it explodes away from you and leaves a coin.

from.quote: Unlike in the Super Mario Bros. subseries, Bob-ombs do not harm the player upon contact. Their explosion, however, damages the player by two wedges of health.
Bob-ombs can be defeated by being kicked or picked up from behind and thrown. This causes them to explode away from the player, leaving behind a coin.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: Their blasts also hurt other enemies nearby, and they come back after you leave the area.

from.quote: Explosions caused by the bombs can also damage other enemies within the blast.
After the player character walks away from the area, the Bob-ombs then respawn.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: A Bob-omb working a cannon does not chase you but still explodes if picked up; the pink Bob-omb Buddies are friendly, give hints and open cannons.

from.quote: These Bob-ombs do not chase the player, but they still explode if picked up.
A pink variant of Bob-omb called a Bob-omb Buddy is introduced in this game.
Bob-omb Buddies are friendly and give the player character helpful hints. They open cannons

sections.name: Chuckya (Wet-Dry World, Tall, Tall Mountain and others)

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A large purple Bob-omb variant that slides about on a metal point and charges you when you come in range; it patrols small areas in Wet-Dry World, Tall, Tall Mountain, Rainbow Ride, the huge side of Tiny-Huge Island and Bowser in the Sky.

from.quote: Chuckyas (also formatted as Chuck-Yas) are a large purple variant of Bob-omb found in Super Mario 64
they move about by sliding across the ground on a metal point
Chuckyas are encountered in Wet-Dry World; on Tall, Tall Mountain; in Rainbow Ride; on Tiny-Huge Island's "huge" portion; and in Bowser in the Sky
When Mario is in range of a Chuckya, it charges towards him
Chuckyas patrol small areas.

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: Pick it up from behind and throw it, and it explodes and releases five coins.

from.quote: To defeat a Chuckya, Mario must pick it up from behind and throw it, causing it to explode and release five coins.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: If it catches you it throws you in a random direction, sometimes a long way or into a pit. You can escape its grasp by pushing the Control Stick from the inside to the outside 11 times before it throws.

from.quote: if a Chuckya catches him, it picks him up and throws him in a random direction
Usually, Mario can be thrown down a far distance or even into a pit.
It is possible to escape from a Chuckya's grasp by pressing and/or pushing the Control Stick from the inside to the outside 11 times before the Chuckya throws Mario.

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A stone slab with an angry face that patrols a small area in Whomp's Fortress and falls on you when you get near; one more waits in Bowser in the Sky.

from.quote: appear in Super Mario 64 as enemies in Whomp's Fortress
with a singular Whomp appearing in Bowser in the Sky
They are large enemies that resemble rectangular stone slabs with snaggletoothed faces
Their faces feature permanently angry expression
Whomps will patrol back and forth in a small area, attempting to slam Mario into the ground for three damage when he gets near.

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: Its only weak spot is its back: let it fall flat, then ground-pound it while it lies there, and it is defeated and releases five coins.

from.quote: They can be defeated by Mario causing them to fall over and subsequently ground-pounding on their sole weak spot, their back
Pounding the Ground on a Whomp while it lies flat will defeat it, which releases five coins.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: Landing on a Whomp's back releases a coin, up to five times. A trick in the original game lets you jump while it falls, pass through it and stand on its back.

from.quote: Landing on the back of a Whomp will release a coin up to five times
A trick in the original version only allows Mario to pass through one and get on its back if he jumps while it falls.

sections.name: Mr. I (Big Boo's Haunt, Lethal Lava Land, Hazy Maze Cave)

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A giant eyeball that turns to follow you and, if left alone, shoots small multicoloured bubbles at you; found in Big Boo's Haunt, Lethal Lava Land and Hazy Maze Cave.

from.quote: It is a giant, usually motionless eyeball that tracks the player character by rotating.
They are found in Big Boo's Haunt, Lethal Lava Land, and the Hazy Maze Cave. They turn to face Mario, shooting small multicolored bubble projectiles at him if undisturbed.

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: Run around it: it shrinks a little trying to keep track of you, is defeated, and drops a blue coin.

from.quote: A Mr. I is defeated if Mario runs around it, causing the Mr. I to shrink slightly from trying to keep track and drop a Blue Coin.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: A larger Big Mr. I waits in the attic of Big Boo's Haunt.

from.quote: The larger Big Mr. I. can be found in the attic of Big Boo's Haunt.

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A red metal box that rolls along set paths over a small tile maze in Shifting Sand Land, trying to flatten you.

from.quote: Tox Boxes are hollow metal boxes that roll along set paths.
Tox Boxes are red, industrial, and metallic boxes with spray-painted faces in Super Mario 64
they are enemies exclusive to Shifting Sand Land
Tox Boxes attempt to flatten Mario by rolling over him. The path is a small maze of tiles surrounded by darker, faster-moving quicksand that sucks Mario in instantly.

lines.label: Weak points
lines.text: It cannot be defeated in the original game. One side of each box is a square hole: stand in it as the box passes over your tile and you survive, but the hole's edges still crush you if you stand under them.

from.quote: While Tox Boxes cannot be defeated in the original Super Mario 64

the last side is a square hole, which is for Mario to stand in as a Tox Box passes over the tile he is standing on, thus letting him survive without being crushed. However, the edges of the holed side still crush Mario if he stands under them.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: Being squashed by a side costs three wedges of health. Long-jumping into a Tox Box's face over the quicksand loses a life at once, as if you had fallen into the quicksand. The maze has a few Red Coins and the course's only cannon.

from.quote: If Mario gets squished by a Tox Box's side, he loses three wedges of health.

Long-jumping into the side of a Tox Box's face that is above quicksand, off the side of the track, makes Mario lose a life instantly, playing the animation as if he has just fallen into the quicksand.
The tiled maze that the Tox Boxes travel on has a few Red Coins on it, as well as the course's only cannon.

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: The collectible star that clears a mission and opens more of the castle; there are 120 in the game.

from.quote: can grant Mario access to more levels in-game
By obtaining a Power Star, the corresponding mission is cleared.
There is a total of 120 Power Stars.

lines.label: Uses
lines.text: The star doors and Big Star Doors in the castle need at least the number of Power Stars shown on them, and 70 are needed to enter Bowser in the Sky. Once you hold all 120, the cannon outside the castle opens and takes you onto its roof.

from.quote: The various ★ doors and Big Star Doors of the Mushroom Castle require Mario to have at least a certain number of Power Stars (which is displayed on normal doors).
A minimum of 70 Power Stars is required to access Bowser in the Sky.
Once Mario collects every Power Star, the cannon outside the Mushroom Castle becomes available for use, giving access to the castle's roof.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: Each course holds seven Power Stars, one of them the secret star for 100 coins, and fifteen stars in all are Secret Stars hidden in secret areas or held by Toads. Eight red coins in a course make a star appear over a Star Marker.

from.quote: There are seven Power Stars in each course; one is a secret Power Star that Mario can obtain from collecting 100 coins
Fifteen of them are Secret Stars, either found in secret areas or held by Toads.
There are eight Red Coins in each course, and collecting all of them causes a Power Star to appear over a Star Marker.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: A star you already have shows as a translucent copy of itself, and collecting it adds nothing to your total.

from.quote: playing the level again turns the Star into a translucent version of itself
This Star can be collected, but it does not add to the player's total Star count.

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A red coin in Super Mario 64 is worth two yellow coins, and eight of them in one area make a Power Star appear over the nearby Star Marker.

from.quote: Each of them are worth two Yellow Coins. When eight Red Coins are collected in an area, a Power Star spawns above the nearby Star Marker.

lines.label: Uses
lines.text: The three cap-switch courses and the three Bowser courses each hold eight, and the two secret courses The Secret Aquarium and Wing Mario Over the Rainbow have one star each from their red coins. The Princess's Secret Slide is the only course with none.

from.quote: all three Cap Switch courses have eight Red Coins to obtain: Tower of the Wing Cap, Cavern of the Metal Cap, and Vanish Cap Under the Moat.
This also goes for the Bowser courses: Bowser in the Dark World, Bowser in the Fire Sea, and Bowser in the Sky.
two secret courses that each have only one Power Star from obtaining Red Coins: The Secret Aquarium and Wing Mario Over the Rainbow.
The Princess's Secret Slide is the only course (secret or otherwise) to lack Red Coins and thus a corresponding Power Star.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: The red coin missions by course: Bob-omb Battlefield, Find the 8 Red Coins; Whomp's Fortress, Red Coins on the Floating Isle; Jolly Roger Bay, Red Coins on the Ship Afloat; Cool, Cool Mountain, Frosty Slide for 8 Red Coins; Big Boo's Haunt, Seek the 8 Red Coins; Hazy Maze Cave, Elevate for 8 Red Coins; Lethal Lava Land, 8-Coin Puzzle with 15 Pieces; Shifting Sand Land, Free Flying for 8 Red Coins.

from.quote: Bob-omb Battlefield - Find the 8 Red Coins
Whomp's Fortress - Red Coins on the Floating Isle
Jolly Roger Bay - Red Coins on the Ship Afloat
Cool, Cool Mountain - Frosty Slide for 8 Red Coins
Big Boo's Haunt - Seek the 8 Red Coins
Hazy Maze Cave - Elevate for 8 Red Coins
Lethal Lava Land - 8-Coin Puzzle with 15 Pieces
Shifting Sand Land - Free Flying for 8 Red Coins

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: The rest: Dire, Dire Docks, Pole-Jumping for Red Coins; Snowman's Land, Shell Shreddin' for Red Coins; Wet-Dry World, Go to Town for Red Coins; Tall, Tall Mountain, Scary 'Shrooms, Red Coins; Tiny-Huge Island, Wiggler's Red Coins; Tick Tock Clock, Stop Time for Red Coins; Rainbow Ride, Coins Amassed in a Maze.

from.quote: Dire, Dire Docks - Pole-Jumping for Red Coins
Snowman's Land - Shell Shreddin' for Red Coins
Wet-Dry World - Go to Town for Red Coins
Tall, Tall Mountain - Scary 'Shrooms, Red Coins
Tiny-Huge Island - Wiggler's Red Coins
Tick Tock Clock - Stop Time for Red Coins
Rainbow Ride - Coins Amassed in a Maze

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A darker blue coin worth five yellow coins.

from.quote: Blue Coins appear in Super Mario 64 and Super Mario 64 DS, where they are depicted with a darker blue color. Blue Coins are worth five Yellow Coins when collected

lines.label: Uses
lines.text: Most come from ground-pounding a Blue Coin Block, and they last only a limited time: once the timer runs out they cannot be collected. Some defeated enemies drop one: Koopa Troopas, Piranha Plants, Boos, Mr. Is, Bookends, Pokeys and the Small Koopa Troopa, and a Grand Goomba gives one only if you kill it with a ground pound.

from.quote: they typically appear from ground-pounding a Blue Coin Block. These Blue Coins appear for a limited time and are unobtainable once the timer expires.

Defeating certain enemies causes a Blue Coin to appear, including Koopa Troopas, Piranha Plants, Boos, Mr. Is, Bookends, Pokeys, and the Small Koopa Troopa. Grand Goombas also give out a Blue Coin if killed using a Ground Pound.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: The blue coins on the slides in Cool, Cool Mountain (one) and Tall, Tall Mountain (three) start to move away from you as you get close, unlike still yellow coins.

from.quote: Blue Coins are also found in the slides on Cool, Cool Mountain (one is present) and Tall, Tall Mountain (three are present), where they start to move away from Mario once he gets close to them, in contrast to the stationary Yellow Coins.

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A mushroom with a green cap and yellow spots that gives an extra life.

from.quote: 1UP Mushrooms are rendered as 2D assets depicted with green caps and yellow spots in Super Mario 64.
Grants an extra life (most appearances)

lines.label: Uses
lines.text: You find them on top of poles, in some yellow blocks, by touching butterflies that are not explosive, in a small field of flowers, and by flying through a ring of coins.

from.quote: They are acquired through a variety of methods, such as on top of poles, in some yellow blocks, from touching butterflies that are not explosive, from a small field of flowers, or from flying through a ring of coins.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: Some stand still, some move away from you and some move at you. Three sit on the roof of the castle.

from.quote: Depending on the 1UP Mushroom, it can be either motionless, move away from Mario, or move at him. There are also three 1UP Mushrooms on the roof of the Mushroom Castle.

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A rare green shell in Super Mario 64 that you can ride for fast travel.

from.quote: Koopa Shells, also referred to as shiny shells (or Shiny Shells), are rare objects in Super Mario 64. They only appear in green

lines.label: Uses
lines.text: Jump on it to travel fast and ram enemies, which defeats them instantly. Riding a shell lets you cross water, lava, quicksand and deadly quicksand without sinking or being hurt, and holding one underwater lets you swim faster for a short while.

from.quote: When Mario jumps on a Koopa Shell, he can travel at fast speed and ram into enemies to defeat them instantly. Riding a shell also allows Mario to navigate over water, lava, quicksand, and deadly quicksand without sinking or being hurt.
if Mario grabs a Koopa Shell while underwater, he can hold the shell in front of him and use it to swim faster in water for a short period of time.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: Shells come from hitting some yellow blocks or from attacking a Koopa Troopa to knock it out of its shell. In the original game the blocks do not refill, but a shell stays until you ride it.

from.quote: can be obtained by hitting some yellow blocks or attacking a Koopa Troopa to get it out of its shell
In the original version, when the player hits the yellow blocks for Koopa Shells, the boxes do not respawn, but shells do not disappear until Mario hitches a ride on one.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: In the Nintendo 64 version of Tiny-Huge Island you can ride the shell on the wind over the Windswept Valley.

from.quote: in Tiny-Huge Island, Mario can use the shell to ride the wind over the Windswept Valley in the Nintendo 64 version

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: Blue cannons in ten courses and one secret stage fire you to places you cannot normally reach, but each stays covered until you find and talk to that course's Bob-omb Buddy.

from.quote: Cannons, this time colored blue, are a vital gameplay element in Super Mario 64 and Super Mario 64 DS.
the player can use it to fire Mario to previously unreachable areas
There is at least one cannon found in ten levels in these games, as well as one secret stage.
The player must successfully locate and talk to the Bob-omb Buddies in each level in order to access the cannon
Until they do, the cannons remain covered by a metal hatch with a picture of a Bob-omb Buddy on it, and are inaccessible.

lines.label: Uses
lines.text: Drop into the hole to climb in, aim with the targeting reticle and press the button to fire. Aim slightly higher than your target, and you take no falling damage from the shot. With a Wing Cap on, you can fly at once after the shot without a triple jump.

from.quote: In order to use the cannon, Mario needs to only drop down into this hole.
a targeting reticle appears on the screen, allowing the player to aim the cannon where they want Mario to go
The player should aim slightly higher than the area they wish to shoot Mario to
Mario will not take falling damage if he is fired from a cannon.

If the player collects a Wing Cap before entering a cannon, the player can fly around as Wing Mario immediately after being fired from the cannon, without needing to perform a Triple Jump to take off first.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: Cannons cannot be unlocked until the first mission is done. In Bob-omb Battlefield one cannon can never be used because it shoots water bombs.

from.quote: Cannons cannot be unlocked until after the first mission is completed.
In Bob-omb Battlefield, there is a cannon controlled by a Bob-omb that Mario can never access due to the cannon shooting water bombs.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: In the Whomp's Fortress mission "Blast Away the Wall" you shoot yourself out of a cannon to smash the top of a nearby wall and free the star.

from.quote: Mario must shoot himself out of a cannon in order to obliterate the topmost section of a nearby wall, which releases the hidden Power Star.
